topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-30, what is the minimum age requirement for an applicant seeking an individual salesperson or broker license in Virginia?
choice_a: At least 18 years of age
choice_b: At least 21 years of age
choice_c: At least 19 years of age
choice_d: There is no minimum age requirement
explanation: 18VAC135-20-30 requires that an applicant for an individual salesperson or broker license be at least 18 years of age.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-30, what general education credential must every individual license applicant hold, apart from completing the required real estate coursework?
choice_a: A high school diploma or its equivalent
choice_b: An associate's degree
choice_c: A bachelor's degree in any field
choice_d: No minimum general education credential is required
explanation: Applicants must hold a high school diploma or its equivalent (such as a GED) in addition to completing the required real estate courses.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-30, what is required of every applicant for an individual real estate license as part of the criminal history background check process?
choice_a: Submission to fingerprinting
choice_b: A notarized personal reference letter
choice_c: A personal credit report
choice_d: An in-person interview with a Board member
explanation: 18VAC135-20-30 requires applicants to submit to fingerprinting as part of the criminal history record check.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-30, which misdemeanor convictions must an applicant disclose to the Board, and within what look-back period?
choice_a: Misdemeanor convictions involving fraudulent or dishonest acts, sexual offenses, drug distribution, or battery, occurring within the preceding 5 years
choice_b: Any misdemeanor conviction of any kind, with no time limit
choice_c: Only misdemeanor convictions occurring within the preceding 1 year
choice_d: Traffic misdemeanors only, within the preceding 3 years
explanation: Applicants must report specified misdemeanor convictions (fraud/dishonesty, sexual offenses, drug distribution, battery) occurring within the 5 years preceding application.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-30, is there a look-back time limit on which felony convictions an applicant must disclose to the Board?
choice_a: No -- all felony convictions must be disclosed regardless of when they occurred
choice_b: Yes -- only felonies within the preceding 10 years
choice_c: Yes -- only felonies within the preceding 5 years
choice_d: Felony convictions never need to be disclosed, only misdemeanors
explanation: Unlike the 5-year look-back for specified misdemeanors, all felony convictions must be disclosed regardless of how long ago they occurred.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-30, what must every applicant sign as part of the license application?
choice_a: A statement verifying the applicant has read and understands the applicable Board regulations and real estate law
choice_b: A waiver of the right to appeal any Board decision
choice_c: A power of attorney designating the Board as the applicant's agent for all purposes
choice_d: A noncompete agreement with the applicant's current employer
explanation: Applicants must sign a statement verifying they have read and understand the provisions of the applicable regulations and the Code of Virginia governing real estate licensees.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-35, how much active salesperson experience must an applicant have to qualify for a broker's license?
choice_a: Active engagement as a real estate salesperson for 36 of the 48 months immediately preceding application
choice_b: Active engagement as a salesperson for 12 of the preceding 24 months
choice_c: Active engagement as a salesperson for 24 consecutive months, no matter when
choice_d: No prior salesperson experience is required if the education requirement is met
explanation: A broker applicant must have been actively engaged as a real estate salesperson for 36 of the 48 months immediately preceding the application.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-35, who must verify a broker applicant's required salesperson experience?
choice_a: The principal or supervising broker for whom the applicant worked at the time the experience was obtained
choice_b: The applicant's real estate school instructor
choice_c: Any currently licensed Virginia broker, regardless of relationship to the applicant
choice_d: A notary public
explanation: The experience must be verified by the principal or supervising broker for whom the applicant worked at the time the experience was obtained.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-35, within what time period before submitting a complete license application must an applicant have passed the required written examination?
choice_a: Within 12 months prior to submitting a complete application
choice_b: Within 6 months prior to submitting a complete application
choice_c: Within 24 months prior to submitting a complete application
choice_d: There is no time limit on how long ago the exam was passed
explanation: An applicant must have passed the required written examination within 12 months prior to submitting a complete license application.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-35, does the Board have discretion to waive the standard education and experience requirements for licensure?
choice_a: Yes, the Board retains discretionary authority to waive these requirements when circumstances warrant
choice_b: No, the education and experience requirements can never be waived
choice_c: Only the education requirement may be waived, never the experience requirement
choice_d: Waivers are available only to applicants who are active-duty military
explanation: The Board retains discretionary authority to waive the education and experience requirements for licensure when circumstances warrant.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-20, a firm that is licensed by the Board and conducts business under a trade or fictitious name must do what regarding that name?
choice_a: Register the trade or fictitious name with the State Corporation Commission
choice_b: Obtain a separate branch office license solely for the name
choice_c: File the name with the local circuit court clerk only, with no state-level filing
choice_d: Nothing further is required beyond the firm license itself
explanation: A licensed firm operating under a trade or fictitious name must register that name with the State Corporation Commission.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-20, which business structures must obtain a firm license separate and distinct from the licenses required of the individuals involved?
choice_a: Nonbroker-owned sole proprietorships, partnerships, associations, LLCs, and corporations
choice_b: Only publicly traded corporations
choice_c: Only entities with more than 10 affiliated licensees
choice_d: None; individual licenses are always sufficient regardless of entity type
explanation: Nonbroker-owned sole proprietorships and other business entities such as partnerships, associations, LLCs, and corporations must secure a firm license distinct from any individual's license.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-20, what must every real estate firm have?
choice_a: A principal broker whose license is active
choice_b: A minimum of three affiliated salespersons
choice_c: A registered agent located outside Virginia
choice_d: An escrow account with a minimum balance of $10,000
explanation: Every real estate firm is required to have a principal broker whose license is active.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-20, when must a principal broker obtain a separate branch office license, and what are examples of locations exempted from that requirement?
choice_a: For each additional business location beyond the primary office, except locations such as a motor vehicle, a P.O. box, a private residence not held out to the public, or a public space like a coffee shop
choice_b: Never; one firm license automatically covers unlimited locations
choice_c: Only if the branch is located in a different city than the main office
choice_d: Only if the branch employs more than five licensees
explanation: A principal broker maintaining more than one place of business must obtain a branch office license for each additional location, subject to specific exceptions such as a vehicle, a P.O. box, a non-public residence, or a public location.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2106.1, what must a group of brokers and/or salespersons operating together as a 'team' obtain?
choice_a: A business entity salesperson license
choice_b: Nothing; teams are exempt from any additional licensing
choice_c: A separate firm license identical to a brokerage's firm license
choice_d: Individual broker licenses for every team member, regardless of experience
explanation: A group of licensees operating together as a team must obtain a business entity salesperson license.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2106.1, for a business entity to obtain a business entity salesperson license, what must be true of its active owners and officers?
choice_a: All active owners and officers must hold a salesperson or broker license
choice_b: At least one owner must hold a broker license, with no restriction on the others
choice_c: Only officers, not owners, must be licensed
choice_d: None of the owners or officers need to be individually licensed if the entity itself is licensed
explanation: All active owners and officers of a business entity seeking a business entity salesperson license must hold a salesperson or broker license.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2106.1, may a real estate team employ unlicensed assistants?
choice_a: Yes, real estate teams may employ unlicensed assistants
choice_b: No, every person affiliated with a team must be individually licensed
choice_c: Only if the assistant is a family member of a team broker
choice_d: Only with prior written Board approval obtained for each individual assistant
explanation: Real estate teams are permitted to employ unlicensed assistants.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2110, what must every resident real estate broker maintain?
choice_a: A place of business in the Commonwealth of Virginia
choice_b: A place of business in the county of the broker's residence only
choice_c: At least two licensed salespersons under direct supervision
choice_d: A separate escrow account for each active listing
explanation: Every resident real estate broker must maintain a place of business in the Commonwealth of Virginia.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2110, when must a nonresident real estate broker maintain a place of business within Virginia?
choice_a: When the broker resides in a state that itself requires Virginia resident brokers to maintain a place of business there
choice_b: In all cases, without exception
choice_c: Never; nonresident brokers are always exempt from any place-of-business requirement
choice_d: Only if the nonresident broker's firm has more than one active Virginia listing
explanation: A nonresident broker must maintain a Virginia place of business only if that broker resides in a state that imposes a reciprocal requirement on Virginia resident brokers.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2111, what must a nonresident applicant for Virginia real estate licensure file with the Real Estate Board?
choice_a: An irrevocable consent allowing suits to be brought against the applicant in the proper Virginia court where the cause of action arises or where the plaintiff resides
choice_b: A surety bond in the amount of $100,000
choice_c: Proof of citizenship in a reciprocal state
choice_d: A notarized letter from the applicant's home-state real estate regulator
explanation: Nonresident applicants must file an irrevocable consent permitting suits against them in the proper Virginia court where the cause of action arises or the plaintiff resides.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2111, through whom may legal process against a nonresident licensee be served, and what must that official do afterward?
choice_a: Through the Director of the Department of Professional and Occupational Regulation, who must file the papers and forward a copy to the licensee's main office by registered mail
choice_b: Through the local sheriff of the county where the Board is located, with no further notice obligation
choice_c: Directly on the licensee only; the Director of DPOR has no role
choice_d: Through the licensee's designated supervising broker only
explanation: Process may be served on the Director of DPOR, who must file it and forward a copy to the licensee's main office by registered mail at the last known address of record.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2109, what must the Real Estate Board receive to initiate the process following a broker's death or disability?
choice_a: Written notification of the broker's death or disability
choice_b: A court order only
choice_c: Verbal notice from any licensee in the firm
choice_d: Nothing; the Board acts automatically 30 days after the event
explanation: The Board must receive written notification of a broker's death or disability to initiate the process under this section.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2109, within how many days must the Board act to approve a successor or appoint an alternate licensed broker to conclude a deceased or disabled broker's business?
choice_a: 30 days
choice_b: 10 days
choice_c: 60 days
choice_d: 180 days
explanation: The Board has 30 days to grant approval to a successor individual or appoint an alternate broker following notification of death or disability.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2109, if a broker did not designate another broker in advance, which of the following is a person the Board may approve to conclude the business, absent an available designated broker?
choice_a: A court-qualified personal representative of the broker's estate
choice_b: Any unlicensed member of the public chosen by the deceased broker's clients
choice_c: The buyer in the broker's most recent pending transaction
choice_d: A broker licensed only in another state, with no Virginia license
explanation: If no designated broker is available, the Board may approve a court-qualified personal representative of the estate, among other statutorily listed options such as an agent under a power of attorney referencing this section, a nominated executor, an adult family member, or an employee or independent contractor of the broker.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2113, what is the initial Real Estate Transaction Recovery Fund assessment charged to each regulant at the time of initial licensure?
explanation: Each initial regulant is assessed $20 at the time of licensure, specifically assigned to the Real Estate Transaction Recovery Fund.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2113, below what minimum balance does the Real Estate Transaction Recovery Fund trigger additional assessments on regulants?
explanation: When the fund balance falls below the $400,000 minimum threshold, regulants may be assessed additional amounts to replenish it.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2113, what is the maximum total amount a regulant may be assessed for the Real Estate Transaction Recovery Fund during any biennial license period?
choice_d: There is no cap
explanation: No regulant may be assessed a total amount of more than $20 during any biennial license period or part thereof.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2113, when the Real Estate Transaction Recovery Fund balance exceeds $2 million, where does the excess go?
choice_a: It is transferred to the Virginia Housing Trust Fund
choice_b: It is refunded pro rata to all licensees
choice_c: It reverts to the Commonwealth's general fund
choice_d: It is transferred to DPOR's general operating budget
explanation: When the fund balance exceeds $2 million, the excess is transferred to the Virginia Housing Trust Fund.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-90, when does a Virginia real estate license generally expire?
choice_a: Two years from the last day of the month in which the license was issued
choice_b: Exactly two years from the calendar date of issuance
choice_c: On June 30 of every even-numbered year, regardless of issuance date
choice_d: One year from the date of issuance
explanation: Salesperson, broker, and firm licenses expire two years from the last day of the month in which they were issued.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-90, when does a concurrent broker license expire?
choice_a: On the same expiration date as the broker's original license, rather than on its own separate two-year cycle
choice_b: One year after the original broker license
choice_c: It never expires as long as the original license remains active
choice_d: 90 days after issuance, and must then be renewed separately every 90 days
explanation: A concurrent broker license expires on the same date as the broker's original license rather than following its own independent two-year expiration cycle.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-110, if a licensee fails to receive the Board's renewal notice before expiration, is the licensee relieved of the duty to renew?
choice_a: No -- failure to receive notice does not relieve the licensee of the obligation to renew
choice_b: Yes, the license is automatically extended until notice is actually received
choice_c: Yes, but only for salespersons, not brokers
choice_d: Yes, if the licensee can show the Board had the correct mailing address on file
explanation: Failure to receive a renewal notice from the Board does not relieve the licensee of the obligation to renew before expiration.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-140, what happens if renewal requirements, including receipt of the fee, are not completed within 30 days of the license's expiration date?
choice_a: The applicable reinstatement fee under 18VAC135-20-15 becomes required
choice_b: The license is permanently revoked with no reinstatement option
choice_c: Nothing changes as long as renewal is completed within 90 days
choice_d: The licensee is automatically referred for disciplinary action
explanation: If renewal, including fee receipt, is not completed within 30 days of expiration, the applicable reinstatement fee becomes required.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-140, for how long after the expiration date may a lapsed license be reinstated upon payment of the reinstatement fee?
choice_a: Up to one year following the expiration date
choice_b: Up to 90 days following the expiration date
choice_c: Up to five years following the expiration date
choice_d: Indefinitely, provided the fee is eventually paid
explanation: A license may be reinstated for up to one year following the expiration date upon payment of the reinstatement fee.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-140, what must an applicant do if more than one year has passed since a license expired?
choice_a: Meet all current educational and examination requirements and apply as a new applicant, since the license may not be reinstated under any circumstances
choice_b: Pay a doubled reinstatement fee and reinstate normally
choice_c: Wait an additional 90 days and then reinstate without any new education
choice_d: Request a hardship waiver directly from the Governor's office
explanation: After one year, the license may not be reinstated under any circumstances; the individual must meet all current educational and examination requirements and apply as a new applicant.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-140, is continuing education required to reinstate a license that was inactive (as opposed to active) at the time it expired?
choice_a: No -- applicants for reinstatement of an inactive license are not required to complete the continuing education requirement for that reinstatement
choice_b: Yes, the full continuing education requirement applies identically whether the lapsed license was active or inactive
choice_c: Only ethics hours are waived; all other continuing education hours are still required
choice_d: Continuing education is waived only if the license was inactive for fewer than 30 days
explanation: Applicants reinstating a lapsed license that was inactive are not required to complete continuing education for that reinstatement -- distinct from separately activating an inactive license, which may still require remedial education under VA Code 54.1-2105.04 if the inactivity exceeded three years.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under the Board's fee schedule at 18VAC135-20-15, what is the total fee for an initial salesperson license by education and examination, once the Real Estate Transaction Recovery Fund assessment is included?
choice_a: $230 ($210 application fee plus a $20 Recovery Fund assessment)
choice_b: $100 flat fee, with no separate assessment
choice_c: $500 ($480 application fee plus a $20 Recovery Fund assessment)
choice_d: $150 ($130 application fee plus a $20 Recovery Fund assessment)
explanation: The initial salesperson license fee by education and examination is $210, plus the $20 Recovery Fund assessment, for a total of $230.
source_note: 18VAC135-20-15 (fee schedule as posted; verify current amount before relying on it, as Board fee schedules are periodically revised)

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under the Board's fee schedule at 18VAC135-20-15, what is the biennial renewal fee for an individual salesperson license?
explanation: The biennial renewal fee for an individual salesperson license is $100.
source_note: 18VAC135-20-15 (fee schedule as posted; verify current amount before relying on it, as Board fee schedules are periodically revised)

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under the Board's fee schedule at 18VAC135-20-15, what is the total fee for an initial broker license by education and examination, once the Recovery Fund assessment is included?
choice_a: $285 ($265 application fee plus a $20 Recovery Fund assessment)
choice_b: $230 ($210 application fee plus a $20 Recovery Fund assessment)
choice_c: $120 flat fee
choice_d: $370 ($350 application fee plus a $20 Recovery Fund assessment)
explanation: The initial broker license fee by education and examination is $265, plus the $20 Recovery Fund assessment, for a total of $285.
source_note: 18VAC135-20-15 (fee schedule as posted; verify current amount before relying on it, as Board fee schedules are periodically revised)

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under the Board's fee schedule at 18VAC135-20-15, what are the reinstatement fees for a lapsed salesperson license versus a lapsed broker license?
choice_a: $155 for a salesperson; $180 for a broker
choice_b: $100 for a salesperson; $120 for a broker (the same as ordinary renewal)
choice_c: $210 for a salesperson; $265 for a broker (the same as an initial application)
choice_d: A flat $50 regardless of license type
explanation: The reinstatement fee is $155 for a lapsed salesperson license and $180 for a lapsed broker license.
source_note: 18VAC135-20-15 (fee schedule as posted; verify current amount before relying on it, as Board fee schedules are periodically revised)

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under the Board's fee schedule at 18VAC135-20-15, what is the total fee for an initial firm license, once the Recovery Fund assessment is included?
choice_a: $370 ($350 application fee plus a $20 Recovery Fund assessment)
choice_b: $240 flat fee
choice_c: $20 flat fee
choice_d: $500 ($480 application fee plus a $20 Recovery Fund assessment)
explanation: The initial firm license fee is $350, plus the $20 Recovery Fund assessment, for a total of $370.
source_note: 18VAC135-20-15 (fee schedule as posted; verify current amount before relying on it, as Board fee schedules are periodically revised)

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2108.1, absent a written agreement to the contrary, by when must a licensee acting on behalf of a landlord deposit rental payments, security deposits, and application deposits into an escrow account?
choice_a: By the end of the fifth business banking day following receipt
choice_b: By the end of the same business day
choice_c: By the end of the tenth calendar day following receipt
choice_d: By the end of the next full calendar month
explanation: Rent payments, security deposits, and application deposits must be placed in an escrow account by the end of the fifth business banking day following receipt, unless otherwise agreed to in writing by the principals to the transaction.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2108.1, can the parties to a lease transaction agree in writing to a deposit timeline for rent and security deposits that differs from the statutory five-business-banking-day default?
choice_a: Yes, the statutory deadline applies 'unless otherwise agreed to in writing by the principals to a lease transaction'
choice_b: No, the five-business-banking-day deadline is mandatory and can never be altered
choice_c: Only a court order can modify the deposit timeline
choice_d: Only the landlord, and not the tenant, may agree to a different timeline
explanation: The statute permits a different deposit timeline where the principals to the lease transaction agree to one in writing.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2108.1, if a single-family home under contract for sale is foreclosed upon and the purchase contract treats the foreclosure as a termination event, may the licensee disburse the earnest money deposit to the purchaser?
choice_a: Yes, without needing additional consent from the other party to the transaction
choice_b: No, a court order is always required first
choice_c: No, the funds must automatically be forfeited to the foreclosing lender
choice_d: Only if the seller separately consents in writing after the foreclosure occurs
explanation: Where the purchase contract treats foreclosure as termination, the licensee may disburse the earnest money to the purchaser without needing additional consent from the other party.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2108.1, when a rental property is foreclosed upon, who is responsible for returning the tenant's security deposit and any accrued interest, and does the prior management contract's terms control?
choice_a: Whoever holds the landlord's interest at the time must return the deposit and accrued interest as required by applicable law, regardless of what the contract says
choice_b: The original property manager remains solely responsible even after losing the management agreement
choice_c: The tenant forfeits the security deposit upon foreclosure
choice_d: The foreclosing lender is never responsible under any circumstances
explanation: Whoever holds the landlord's interest at the time of foreclosure must return the tenant's security deposit and accrued interest as required by applicable law, regardless of contractual arrangements.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2108.1, what happens to an existing property management agreement when the managed property is foreclosed upon?
choice_a: It converts to a month-to-month arrangement, with the original terms continuing to govern unless the parties agree otherwise
choice_b: It is automatically and permanently terminated with no further obligations for either party
choice_c: It transfers unmodified to the foreclosing lender for the remainder of its original term
choice_d: It becomes void and must be entirely renegotiated before any further rent may be collected
explanation: Foreclosure converts an existing property management agreement into a month-to-month arrangement, with the original terms continuing to govern unless modified by the parties.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2108.1, what protection does a licensee have who complies with the statute's escrow and foreclosure-related provisions?
choice_a: Immunity from liability, absent gross negligence or intentional misconduct
choice_b: No protection; the licensee bears strict liability regardless of compliance
choice_c: Immunity only if the licensee also carries a minimum $1 million errors-and-omissions policy
choice_d: Immunity only for transactions under $200,000
explanation: A licensee who complies with the statute's provisions is granted immunity from liability in the absence of gross negligence or intentional misconduct.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2108, what may the Real Estate Board do if it has reason to believe a licensee cannot adequately protect the public's interest in funds held in escrow?
choice_a: Petition a court of record, which may temporarily enjoin the licensee's activity and appoint a receiver to conserve, protect, and disburse the funds
choice_b: Immediately seize the licensee's personal bank accounts without any court involvement
choice_c: Notify the licensee's clients only, with no further Board action available
choice_d: Refer the matter exclusively to the Attorney General for criminal prosecution, bypassing civil remedies
explanation: The Board may petition a court of record, which may temporarily enjoin the licensee and appoint a receiver to conserve, protect, and disburse escrow funds.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2108, who normally pays the costs and fees of a court-appointed receiver over a licensee's escrow funds, and when does the Board instead pay?
choice_a: The licensee normally pays; the Board pays if the court finds the licensee acted without fault and violated neither the statute nor Board regulations
choice_b: The Board always pays receiver costs regardless of the licensee's fault
choice_c: The client whose funds are held always pays the receiver's costs
choice_d: Receiver costs are split evenly between the Board and the licensee in every case
explanation: Receiver costs are normally paid by the licensee, but the Board pays them from its own funds if the court finds the licensee acted without fault and violated neither the statute nor Board regulations.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-181, when must a licensee disclose to the principals how interest earned on an interest-bearing escrow account will be disbursed?
choice_a: In the contract of purchase or lease, in writing, at the time the contract or lease is written
choice_b: Only if a principal specifically requests it after closing
choice_c: Disclosure of interest disbursement is never required under this regulation
choice_d: Only verbally, at the final walk-through
explanation: Written disclosure of how interest will be disbursed must be made to the principals in the contract of purchase or lease at the time it is written.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-181, earnest money deposits in a purchase transaction must be deposited, handled, and disbursed in accordance with which statute?
choice_b: VA Code 54.1-2113
choice_c: VA Code 54.1-2130
choice_d: VA Code 54.1-2100
explanation: 18VAC135-20-181 provides that purchase-transaction earnest money must be deposited, handled, and disbursed in accordance with VA Code 54.1-2108.2.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-181, what must be true of an escrow account's balance with respect to all funds designated to be held by the firm?
choice_a: The account must maintain sufficient balances at all times for all funds designated to be held by the firm
choice_b: The account balance may run temporarily negative if reconciled by month's end
choice_c: There is no minimum balance requirement as long as records are accurate
choice_d: The balance must always exceed $50,000
explanation: The regulation requires that escrow accounts maintain sufficient balances at all times for all funds that are designated to be held by the firm.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-185, for how long must a brokerage agreement be retained, and from what date does that period run?
choice_a: Three years from the date of execution
choice_b: One year from the date of execution
choice_c: Three years from the date of closing only, never from execution
choice_d: Indefinitely, with no permitted disposal date
explanation: A brokerage agreement must be retained for three years from the date of execution.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-185, for how long must a disclosure and consent to dual agency or dual representation be retained?
choice_a: Three years from the date of execution
choice_b: Five years from the date of execution
choice_c: Only for the duration of the listing agreement itself
choice_d: Retention of dual agency disclosures is not required under this regulation
explanation: Each disclosure and consent to dual agency or dual representation must be retained for three years from the date of execution.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-185, for how long must a complete and accurate record of receipts and disbursements of money received on behalf of others be retained, and from what triggering event does that period run?
choice_a: Three years from the closing date, the termination of the sales transaction, or the conclusion of the licensee's lease-related involvement
choice_b: One year from the date of the initial deposit only
choice_c: Three years from the date the escrow account itself was first opened, regardless of individual transactions
choice_d: Such records need not be retained once the transaction closes
explanation: Records of receipts and disbursements of money received on behalf of others must be retained for three years from the closing date, contract termination, or conclusion of the lease-related involvement, as applicable.
